DEVELOPMENT PLAN REVIEW BOARD
  MINUTES
  JANUARY 23, 2025 AT 8:30 AM
  245 EAST BONITA AVENUE
  COUNCIL CHAMBER CONFERENCE ROOM

  BOARD MEMBERS PRESENT

  David Bratt, Planning Commission
  Scott Dilley, Chamber of Commerce
  Brad McKinney, City Manager
  Steve Barragan, Engineering Manager (substitute for Shari Garwick)
  Luis Torrico, Director of Community Development

  STAFF PRESENT

  Marco Espinoza, Planning Manager
  Yasmin Dabbous, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Galindo, Assistant Planner
  Byron Luk, Planning Intern
  Caitlyn Cortez, Administrative Assistant

CALL TO ORDER

Mr. Bratt called the regular meeting of the Development Plan Review Board to order at 8:33 a.m.
so as to conduct regular business in the Council Chamber Conference Room.

DPRB ITEMS

DPRB 1. DPRB 24-16; PROJ 24-57

A request to decrease the front yard setback from twenty (20} feet to zero (0) feet in order to install
a front yard fence that would be five (5) to six (6) feet in height at 1006 Via Romales (APN: 8448-
056-008), located within the Specific Plan No. 12 (SP-12}, Area I Zone.

Assistant Planner Dabbous presented the staff report and recommended the Board approve
DPRB 24-16; PROJ 24-57.

Assistant Planner Dabbous stated she has passed around a revision to the Conditions of
Approval. Condition No. 17 on page eight of the packet will be revised to say, "The driveway
automatic gate shall not be installed within eighteen ( 18) feet from the back of the existing
sidewalk to allow for queuing". An additional condition will be added to say that the revised front
yard setback is for the installation of fencing only and will not be applicable to any new buildings
or structures.

Engineering Manager Barragan stated in regard to revised Condition No. 17, the City does
require fifteen feet from the face of the curb for line of sight, but for queuing they are requiring
eighteen feet behind the sidewalk to allow the vehicle to be on the property and not block the
sidewalk and street. A standard-size parking spot is nine by eighteen feet so that is why they are
 DPRB Minutes
January 23, 2025  Page 2

using the eighteen-foot measurement. The fencing can stay the same, but the gate needs to be
set back. Currently, the gate is about thirteen feet behind the sidewalk, so it needs to be moved
back five feet.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated they are allowing the fence to be up to the property line, but
the plans show they are currently placing it on the concrete curb, following the grass line. This
approval will allow the homeowner flexibility to move the fence to the property line without the
need to come back to DPRB for another approval.

Engineering Manager Barragan stated the property line is eight feet behind curb face so its
three feet behind sidewalk so even if the fence was at the property line, the rendering would not
be correct.

Director of Community Development Torrico confirmed that the condition as written is eighteen
feet behind the sidewalk and that is correct.

Engineering Manager Barragan stated that is correct, as long as a vehicle can come out of the
gate without blocking sidewalk.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated that when the applicant submits a new drawing, they will
show the sidewalk at five feet with the additional three feet off the sidewalk for public property.

Mr. Dilley asked if the fence can be at a zero setback as long as the gate is set back the eighteen
feet.

Mr. Bratt stated that the applicant plans to move the whole fence back, but the only thing that is
required to move back is the gate. Mr. Bratt then asked what is surrounding the rest of the property
to keep the home safe.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated they have existing retaining walls and block walls that range
from five to six feet high surrounding the rest of the property,

The Applicant confirmed the height of the walls varies.

Engineering Manager Barragan asked if the walls are visible from the street.

The Applicant stated no, they are not.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated he knows the Board in the past has
approved similar requests and asked what the standards are for those similar projects.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated the fences run around five to six feet and placement would
typically be at the property line with gates at setbacks. These projects are located in the
Gainsborough and Calle Cristina areas.

The Applicant delivered a speech depicting the burglary of his home while his family was in the
residence. The burglars jumped the block wall, and he feels with the addition of the fence it would
 DPRB Minutes
January 23, 2025  Page 3

deter future situations. The applicant requested his project be approved as proposed without the
gate setback from the fence.

Speaker 1 (The Contractor)- stated there isn't a lot of traffic on this cul-de-sac, and if the
applicant has guests, he can leave the gate open so there isn't a queuing issue.

Mr. Bratt asked if the eighteen-foot setback is a policy or code.

Engineering Manager Barragan stated the home is in Planning Area One which has flexibility
because of the different topography of each lot. If you look in the code, it says eighteen feet from
back of sidewalk so that is where this decision came from. He stated the Applicant brought up
good points about the existing gates in the area, but just because they are existing doesn't mean
they should continue that same process.

Mr. Dilley stated he prefers the gate as proposed but does not like the zero setback for the
fencing. He stated there should be a buffer between the sidewalk and fencing. He proposes in
this case, they can approve a fifteen-foot setback for the gate, due to the topography, but in the
future, they should keep the eighteen-foot setback.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated he does not like the zero-foot setback but
does agree with the five-foot setback for the fencing. He stated that in terms of the gate, there are
ways to install it to allow for the eighteen feet that will not impact the design.

City Manager McKinney stated he does not like the zero-foot setback for the fence and while he
understands the aesthetics issue, he agrees with Public Works and wants to keep the cars off the
sidewalk.

Director of Community Development Torrico moved to approve the request subject to the
revised conditions requiring the gate to be minimum of eighteen feet from back of sidewalk and
reducing the fence setback to five feet.

The Applicant asked to clarify the change in conditions.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated the eight feet from the back of the sidewalk
where his fence is proposed is okay, for future they are removing the zero-foot setback and are
changing that to five feet. They will still require the eighteen-foot setback for the gate.

The Applicant stated the slope of the driveway is too steep to open the gates if it is set back
eighteen feet. With their proposal as is, it's as far away from the sidewalk as they can get without
their gate having to open at an upward angle. The distance from back of sidewalk to the pillar is
eight feet so the gate might be set back to nine feet. He stated that on his cul-de-sac there is zero
traffic, and his house is the last house on the cul-de-sac.

Mr. Dilley stated they have to be careful with this approval because the board would be setting a
precedent for future submittals for other properties.

The Applicant asked the Board if they would allow for zero setback for the gate so there is no
option for a car on the sidewalk.
 DPRB Minutes
January 23, 2025  Page 4

Engineering Manager Barragan stated that a zero-foot setback creates a line-of-sight issue for
someone walking down the sidewalk. As the angle changes, the visibility through the fencing
becomes non-existent.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated that if there is a large slope the gate then has to lift up in the
air and it complicates the project.

The Applicant asked if the Board allows a zero-foot setback for the fence, will they allow the gate
to be at zero and clarified that they will only have two pillars eighteen inches wide and doesn'.t
think this will cause a visibility issue.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated they prefer the setback at the eight-foot
setback at landscaping as originally proposed. He then asked the applicant if they can make
fifteen feet from the face of the curb work for the gate.

The Applicant stated yes, that is the original proposal.

Mr. Bratt stated that the original intent was to put the fence around the grass line which would
allow for fifteen feet from face of curb. He stated he does not like to set precedent, but he believes
it's a fair compromise to follow the natural contour. Because there is no foot traffic, he is willing to
work with the original proposal.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated they can write in the conditions that this approval is solely
approved for this home's topography and that these approvals are case by case.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated he would like to add to the condition that
this project was approved based on the topography of this home's location.

Planning Manager Espinoza confirmed with the Board that there is no change to Condition No.
17.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated he would revise his previous motion to
approve the project subject to the addition of a condition that states the revised front yard setback
of five (5) feet is for in installation of new fencing only. The reduced setback is not applicable to
the construction or placement of any new buildings, structures, etc. They can move the fence up
to five (5) feet from property line, but the gate cannot move from the approved setback.

Planning Manager Espinoza stated they will modify Condition No. 17 to state the fence can
move up to five feet from the property line but the gate can't be moved from the current proposed
locations.

Motion:

Director of Community Development Torrico moved to approve DPRB 24-16 with the following
revisions to the Conditions of Approval.

  1. Add a condition that states the revised front yard setback of five (5) feet is for the
  installation of fencing only. The reduced setback is not applicable to the construction or
  placement of any new buildings, structures, etc.
 DPRB Minutes
January 23, 2025  Page 5

Motion seconded by Mr. Dilley.

Motion carried 5-0.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

No communications were made .

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business the meeting was adjourned at 9:20 a.m. to the meeting of April
24, 2025

  David Bratt, Chairman
  Development Plan Review Board

   DEVELOPMENT PLAN REVIEW BOARD
  MINUTES
  JANUARY 9, 2025 AT 8:30 AM
  245 EAST BONITA AVENUE
  COUNCIL CHAMBER CONFERENCE ROOM

  BOARD MEMBERS PRESENT

  David Bratt, Planning Commission
  Scott Dilley, Chamber of Commerce
  Brad McKinney, City Manager
  Shari Garwick, Director of Public Works
  Luis Torrico, Director of Community Development

  STAFF PRESENT

  Marco Espinoza, Planning Manager
  Yasmin Dabbous, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Galindo, Assistant Planner
  Byron Luk, Planning Intern
  Caitlyn Cortez, Administrative Assistant

CALL TO ORDER

David Bratt called the regular meeting of the Developmental Plan Review Board to order at 8:33
a.m. so as to conduct regular business in the Council Chamber Conference Room.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

1. Approved October 24, 2024 minutes.

  Moved by City Manager McKinney, seconded by Director of Community Development
  Torrico to approve the October 24, 2024 Development Plan Review Board minutes. Motion
  carried 5-0.

2. Approved November 26, 2024 minutes.

  Moved by City Manager McKinney, seconded by Director of Community Development
  Torrico to approve the November 26, 2024 Development Plan Review Board minutes. Motion
  carried 5-0.

DPRB ITEMS

DPRB 1. Tree Permit 24-26; ACCELA PROJ-24-51

A request to remove two hundred and thirty-four (234) mature trees located within the common
areas of Via Verde Ridge HOA. The site is located within Specific Plan - 11 Zone (APN: 8448-
008-053)
 DPRB Minutes
January 9, 2025  Page 2

Planning Intern Luk presented the staff report and recommended the Board approve TRP 24-
26 subject to the Conditions of Approval in Attachment 1.

Planning Intern Luk stated that at the last DPRB meeting, the HOA mentioned a phasing plan
for the tree removal and the staff report was not changed to reflect the phasing plan so as not to
create discrepancies between the two staff reports. The applicant, Mike Long, would like to do a
phasing plan of three years at a rate of seventy-eight (78) trees per year based on budgeting.
Staff would like to modify Condition No. 13 and Condition No. 14 in the Conditions of Approval to
address the tree removal phasing plan. Additionally, staff has received ten (10) emails in support
of the tree removal. He asked if the applicant would like to share the HOA Board's efforts to inform
the Via Verde Ridge community of the tree removal permit since the last DPRB meeting.

The Applicant stated that the HOA board has an e-blast system they used to email the
community a list of trees being removed and a link to the website for Arbor Map. They also
physically numbered all the trees and flagged the trees with a red ribbon for easier visibility. They
had two HOA meetings and at the December meeting they did an extensive overview and public
discussion. The general consensus of the residents was supportive of the tree removal. He feels
that the HOA Board did everything possible to explain the proposed project and to allow residents
the opportunity to comment. He stated that they held a meeting yesterday and no one came to
oppose the tree removals.

Director of Public Works Garwick asked if the City has a plan for replacement trees.

Planning Intern Luk stated no, there is not a replacement plan.

Director of Public Works Garwick asked the HOA Board if they have a replacement plan.

Speaker 1- John Begin stated no, the trees are all in the common landscaped area and they are
overgrown. He stated he believes that when they remove the trees, they may want to replace
some of them. They want to make the decision on where, when, and what type of tree in the
future. They also want to see the area once its removed, so they have better visibility on what
needs to be done. He stated the fires happening now (Pacific Palisades and Altadena) are a good
example of what can happen in Via Verde. The current windstorm took down multiple tall trees in
the Vons Shopping Center. He stated the trees are too close to the homes and will take out the
entire house to the driveways if they fall. He stated they need to do something about this problem
before a disaster happens.

Director of Public Works Garwick asked the HOA Board if a resident wants to plant more trees,
can they submit a request to the HOA Board.

Speaker 1 stated yes.

Director of Community Development Torrico asked if the HOA Board anticipates coming
forward in the future with additional removals.

Speaker 1 stated no, that's not in the plans.

Speaker 2 stated she lives near the golf course and the trees have been preventing the golf balls
from coming into her yard. She had broken windows in the past and it's too dangerous without
the trees blocking the way. She lives off Puente Street and would like to keep her Sycamore trees.
 DPRB Minutes
January 9, 2025  Page 3

The Applicant stated they will only be removing the trees on the back side of her home, and this
will not impact her regarding the golf balls.

Speaker 1 stated there are eight houses on Puente Street and the trees on the south side are
not common area trees, they are either City trees or private trees that the HOA does not maintain.

Speaker 2 stated that as long as they don't remove her front trees, she is happy with the plan.

Speaker 3 - Catherine Begin stated she would like to thank the Public Works Department for
taking down the tree by the retirement home. She stated she is from the Safety Committee and
was the person who sent in a public comment email with multiple names listed in favor of the tree
removal. She stated the HOA did not have a tree plan in the past and in the last three years the
Board has worked hard to come up with one to keep everyone safe. They had a tree fall on a
neighbor's home into the kitchen and John was the first one there to help clean up. She stated
she is part of the CERT team and is receiving calls from the community stating they are worried
about fires and children playing in the yards as well as the cost of water to maintain the trees.
They would like the City to work in partnership with the HOA and feel they have a good handle on
the neighborhood. She stated other HOA's are having the same problems and next year Cal Fire
will come in and ask to remove trees and this will continue to cause future problems. She stated
Via Verde is in the highest fire zone.

Speaker 4 stated he is the Treasurer from the Hillview HOA and their homes are in the same
situation as Via Verde Ridge. They have two thousand trees and due to lack of maintenance over
the years the trees are overgrown. He stated that today they have a contractor going to a home
where a one-hundred-foot pine tree fell into their yard and damaged the roof of their home. He
stated they focus on dangerous trees, but they don't have the budget to maintain all of the trees
to keep them safe. The trees are right up against the back fences and were planted forty years
ago. He is there in support of Via Verde Ridge and the relief the City can give them in terms of
removing trees. He stated with one hundred and sixty homes and two thousand trees his
community does not want to plant anymore if they decide to remove them.

Speaker 5 stated he lives on Via Esperanza and has a one-hundred-foot-tall tree that is thirty feet
away from his home and he is in full support of the tree removal. He saw several trees fall down
during the windstorm and some of them had red tags on them.

Director of Community Development Torrico asked if the tree near his home is on the removal
list.

Speaker 5 stated that he's not sure if the tree is on the list.

Director of Community Development Torrico stated that before voting he recommends
amending Condition No. 13 to address the phasing removal plan and recommends striking
Condition No. 14 to eliminate the applicant needing to submit photos of the removed trees within
two hundred and seventy days of approval. He also suggested adding a condition that provides
additional protection for the City and requires the HOA to call the City for approval prior to cutting
any trees adjacent to the sidewalk to confirm they are not City trees.

The Applicant stated they are currently working with the City Arborist and will go through the list
to verify they don't tag City trees. They believe some City trees are currently tagged, and they will
remove the tags and mark them clearly indicating they belong to the City.
 DPRB Minutes
January 9, 2025  Page 4

Motion: Tree Permit 24-26

Director of Community Development Torrico moved to approve TRP 24-26 with the following
revisions to the Cond itions of Approval :

  1. Amend Condition No . 13 to address the phasing plan of three years at a rate of seventy-
  eight trees per year.

  2. Strike Condition No. 14.

  3. Add a condition that provides additional protection for the City and requires the HOA to
  call the City for approval prior to cutting any trees adjacent to the sidewalk to confirm they
  are not City trees and that if there are trees next to sidewalk, the Board will check with city
  before removal.

Motion seconded by Director of Public Works Garwick.

Motion carried 5-0.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

No communications were made.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business the meeting was adjourned at 9:01 a.m . to the meeting of April
24, 2025.

  David Bratt, Chairman
  Development Plan Review Board
